contract: Read one preloaded finite TS188 or M2TS192 entity with one DVB DTS-HD elementary stream, one extension substream and no core. ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 F.4.3 permits multiple complete access units in an aligned finite PES only for a single substream.

The reference opens the MPEG-TS demuxer with NOPARSE and NOFILLIN, without stream discovery or decoding. The pinned demuxer reports the DVB DTS-HD descriptor as bin_data; this operation explicitly invokes the public DTS parser on each original PES, drains it at the finite boundary, and verifies contiguous, byte-identical coverage of every PES byte. The legacy parser-enabled demux comparison remains separate.

Compare every access unit's payload, stream index and PID, elementary range, intersection within the original PES, physical PES header and carrier positions, declared PES length, original header bytes and raw PTS/DTS. Feed the parser the original source clocks: only the first access unit claims the PES anchor, and a missing DTS remains missing.

Compare the exact reduced coded duration from Table 7-2 reference-clock metadata of the lowest-index extension, including unknown and inherited metadata. The reference caller reads this fixed prefix independently from the source bytes; FFmpeg's duration inferred from the opaque asset body is not this source field. These authored headers test framing, not decoder conformance.

Controls include one access unit per PES, varying grouped counts and sizes, short and long headers, a nonzero substream index, PTS-only, PTS/DTS and untimed PES, and unknown, inherited and late static timing. Inputs are generated by cargo xtask fixture transport-dts-hd-grouped and cargo xtask fixtures; no generated media is committed.
